name: Oxfam America
mission:
Oxfam is a global organization that fights inequality to end poverty and injustice. We offer lifesaving
support in times of crisis and advocate for economic justice, gender equality, and climate action. We
demand equal rights and equal treatment so that everyone can thrive, not just survive. The future is
equal.
theoryOfChange: We see a future in which no one lives in poverty. We can get there by taking an integrated approach, working together to combat poverty on all levels.

dimension_explanations.alignment: This charity is a strong fit for donors interested in humanitarian causes and has a long history of successful work [11]. It is sadaqah-eligible and focuses on urgent needs like disaster response and gender justice [2]. It spends $0.19 per $1 raised on fundraising, which is within a reasonable range for large international groups [12].
dimension_explanations.impact: Oxfam America is highly effective, reaching beneficiaries at a cost of about $4.02 each [2]. The organization provides strong evidence of its success, such as resolving job grievances and helping pass major laws in Ghana and Tanzania [10][7][9]. While its program expense ratio is moderate at 71.7%, its governance and financial health are very strong [1][12].

baseline_narrative.headline: Oxfam America provides humanitarian relief and fights poverty by empowering local communities and advocating for fair laws.
strengths: High impact with a low cost of approximately $4.02 per beneficiary
Strong track record of passing legislative amendments and governance bills in multiple countries
Maintains 8.0 months of working capital to ensure stable operations
baseline_narrative.summary: Oxfam America works with local partners to provide emergency aid and promote gender justice across the globe [2]. In FY2025, the organization managed $75,339,434 in total revenue to support its mission of helping families play a central role in their own development [12]. The charity maintains an overall score of 96.0/100 from Charity Navigator for its performance and accountability [1].

strengths.detail: Delivers core emergency relief and local development programs at a low cost of approximately $4.02 per beneficiary.
Maintains a <cite id="1">96/100 overall score from Charity Navigator</cite> and holds the Platinum Seal of Transparency from Candid.
Successfully advocated for the passage of <cite id="7">major legislative governance bills</cite> and parliamentary amendments across multiple operating countries.
strengths.point: Proven Systems and Policy Track Record

strengths_deep_dive: Oxfam America excels at combining immediate direct relief with structural policy reform. Their programs reach millions of beneficiaries globally at an extraordinary efficiency rate of $4.02 per individual [3]. On governance, independent evaluations confirm that Oxfam's advocacy has directly influenced national laws, including securing <cite id="7">legislative governance bills</cite> in Ghana and achieving <cite id="9">parliamentary adoption of CSO legislative amendments</cite> in Tanzania [7], [9]. Additionally, the organization holds <cite id="1">a 96/100 overall score from Charity Navigator</cite>, backed by 8.0 months of working capital reserves that provide long-term stability [1].
rich_narrative.summary: Founded in 1942, Oxfam America operates as a major global relief and development organization that partners with local groups to fight poverty and advocate for systemic change [2]. The organization works across regions including North America, Europe, Asia, Africa, and South America [2]. In FY2025, Oxfam America generated <cite id="2">$75,339,434 in total revenue</cite> to support emergency aid, climate action, and gender justice initiatives [12]. The charity earns high operational trust, holding a <cite id="1">96/100 overall score from Charity Navigator</cite> [1]. However, donors should note that its program expense ratio stands at 71.7% in FY2025 filings, which sits below the peer median [12]. Despite this, the charity maintains incredible reach, delivering direct services at a low cost of roughly $4.02 per beneficiary across various emergency and development programs [3]. Furthermore, evaluation reports show concrete institutional impacts, such as passing <cite id="7">legislative governance bills</cite> and supporting local community resilience [7].
